[BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | Too weak to climb Abu Jahl’s chest, Ibn Masʿūd used a ploy; Abu Jahl called him a shepherdling, and Ibn Masʿūd replied that Islam prevails and is not prevailed over.

[BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · ابن الشيخ | reports | Ibn al-Shaykh says naṣiya can mean the forehead hair or the place where it grows, and here it stands for the face and head; Abu Jahl meticulously groomed his forelock.
[BURSEVI:v10p366/r10] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The threat is to drag Abu Jahl by his forelock into Hell through the torment angels, humiliating him; Arabs treated seizure by the forelock as degrading subjugation.
[BURSEVI:v10p366/r11] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | In ʿAyn al-Maʿānī, taking someone by the forelock is an expression of coercion and humiliation.
[BURSEVI:v10p366/r12] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The forelock may also signify Abu Jahl being dragged face-first at Badr, when Muslims were enabled to seize him after he resumed forbidding prayer.
[BURSEVI:v10p366/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The oath-prefixed warning means that unless he stops, desists, repents, and submits before death, God will seize him by the forelock.

[ALUSI:96:16/r1] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | Nāṣiyatin is an appositive to the definite al-nāṣiya; the adjective makes the indefinite informative. Basrans require only informative value for indefinite apposition, while Kufans also require matching wording and an adjective.
[ALUSI:96:16/r2] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | Calling the forelock a liar and sinner intensifies the owner's traits, as if each part lied and sinned; this is figurative attribution of a whole's quality to a part, like 16:62 and the idiom that a face describes beauty. | mentions 16:62

[ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Nāṣiyatin is an appositive to the definite nāṣiya; its modifiers make the indefinite informative. Basrans require informativeness, while Kufans require matching form and a descriptive modifier.

[ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Nasiyah means the hair or forelock on the forehead and can also name the forehead or front of the head; here it is a metonym for the head and therefore the person.
[ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The indefinite apposition generalizes the threat; “lying, sinful” both justifies the dragging and clarifies that the person, who actually lies and sins, is meant, though the literal forelock remains possible too.
[QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | Safʿ means seizing violently; the forehead is the arrogant tyrant's raised, forward, conspicuous part.
[QUTB-ZILAL:96:16/r1] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | This lying, sinful forehead deserves to be seized and cast down; the wording evokes the moment of violent seizure and overthrow.
[IBNASHUR:96:16/r1] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Nāṣiyah is an appositive to the forelock, made indefinite to refer to the class: a forelock of the lying, erring kind.
[IBNASHUR:96:16/r2] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Khāṭiʾah is the active participle of khaṭiʾa, to commit a sin; calling the forelock a liar and sinner is a rational metaphor for its owner.
[IBNASHUR:96:16/r3] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The personification imagines the owner's lies and sins visibly emerging from his forehead, making the forelock fit for seizure.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The added bāʾ strengthens the sense of contact in the seizure; the light emphatic nūn commonly follows positive oaths and is written as an alif to reflect pausal pronunciation.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The light emphatic nūn often enters affirmative oaths and is written as an alif in the muṣḥaf to reflect its pronunciation at pause.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The second “kalla” reinforces the first; placing one at the start created suspense, and the closing position is the natural place for its counterpart.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Seizing means gripping and pulling forcefully; taking someone by the forelock signifies dragging him to punishment and humiliating him.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The definite forelock is anaphoric, meaning the forelock of the man who forbids prayer; Kufan grammarians call the lām a substitute for the genitive pronoun, while Basrans posit an attachment for the lām’s complement. | mentions 96:9, 96:10
